📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, losing weight in your 50s, even a modest amount, may help protect your heart health later in life, according to latest research.Adults who lost weight in their early 50s saw their blood pressure, “good” cholesterol and inflammation change at about the same rate as adults who stayed at a healthy weight, according to a study from researchers at University College London and the University of Glasgow.Adults who gained weight in their early 50s saw those same measures worsen faster by their early 60s, the researchers reported. The authors posted the study on a research-sharing website on September 4. Other scientists have not yet peer-reviewed the work.

Industry observers note that charis Bridger-Staatz, PhD, a senior research fellow at UCL, led the study. She told Healthline the main takeaway for adults over 50 was that “it’s not too late to try and do things that are going to improve your health.”Nearly half of U.S. adults ages 40 to 59 had obesity from 2021 to 2023, the highest rate of any adult age group, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Among all U.S. adults, around 31.7% were overweight, according to the CDC.

The findings can apply to Americans because British and U.S. adults share similar weight patterns, said Solveig Cunningham, PhD, a professor of global health at Emory University’s Rollins School of Public Health. Cunningham, who was not involved in the research, told Healthline that Americans tend to gain weight across adulthood.

According to recent reports, “By the time you get into your 50s, close to the majority of Americans already have obesity. Many others have overweight,” she said.The World Health Organization (WHO) calls obesity a chronic disease. Healthcare professionals diagnose overweight and obesity using a person’s weight and height, or body mass index (BMI).

Bridger-Staatz said the team set out to learn who lost weight and kept it off before GLP-1 weight loss medications became available, and whether that weight loss improved health over time.

She remarked researchers had long assumed that “once people had become overweight or developed obesity, people didn’t really lose weight and certainly not sustained it.”The team also asked, she said, “can we try and say something positive about health that isn’t just this kind of like doom and gloom?”The researchers used the British 1958 National Child Development Study, which has followed about 17,500 people born during one week in 1958. Of those, 6,309 took part in a health check in their early 60s, according to the report.The team compared each person’s highest weight between ages 23 and 42 with their weight between ages 50 and 55. Researchers sorted people by whether they gained or lost more than 5% of their body weight and kept the change. For a 200-pound person, 5% equals 10 pounds.To track heart health, the team compared blood tests and blood pressure readings at ages 44 and 62 with those of people who maintained a healthy weight.“We know everyone’s heart health is kind of going to get a little bit worse over that time because you are aging and that’s expected,” Bridger-Staatz said. The question, she said, was, “Does it slow the rate at which people’s heart health is getting worse?”.

Weight loss slowed the decline in heart health for people who were overweight and for people with obesity, according to the report.People who were overweight and lost weight had the strongest positive results. By age 62, their body fat-to-lean tissue ratio matched that of the healthy-weight group. The authors wrote that differences in body fat may partly explain why weight changes affected heart health.People with obesity who lost weight had less body fat at 62 than people in the other obesity groups, according to the report.Sudhakara Chennareddy, MD, prevention cardiologist in the Center for Cardiovascular Prevention, Metabolism and Lipids at Georgia Heart Institute, told Healthline those results are what he’d expect. He was not involved in the research.“Even losing 5% has beneficial effects on the cardiovascular side effects,” he remarked. Long-term blood sugar was the exception. For people with obesity who lost weight, it rose more than in the healthy-weight group, though the authors reported that the result was not statistically significant.

A 2025 study of more than 15,000 U.S. adults, published in Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, found that adults who had previously had obesity tended to have higher blood sugar than those who had never had it, even after their BMI dropped.

Sources indicate that “It’s not the patient’s fault… We need to treat this one like any other chronic disease, like we treat hypertension or we treat diabetes,” Chennareddy noted.Compared with the healthy-weight group, people who gained weight in their early 50s had faster increases in blood pressure, blood fats, and inflammation, and declines in “good” cholesterol. Obesity is a chronic metabolic disease that leads to inflammation in the body, which can raise the risk of heart attack and stroke and worsen cholesterol levels, Chennareddy said. “The more weight they gain, they develop prediabetes and diabetes and fatty liver disease as well,” he said.These changes were largest for people who developed obesity or already had obesity and gained more weight, the researchers reported. This group also saw faster increases in long-term blood sugar levels.About 37% of participants gained more than 5% of their body weight in their early 50s. Only about 6% lost weight and kept it off, according to the study.“To me, that’s sort of the stronger message,” Cunningham said of the findings. Her advice for adults in their 50s is to avoid gaining weight.

People with obesity who lost and then gained the weight back saw faster drops in “good” cholesterol and faster rises in inflammation and long-term blood sugar.

By age 62, they weighed slightly less, on average, than people whose obesity remained steady, according to the report’s data. They also carried more body fat and had more inflammation.Weight cycling can do more harm than steady weight, Chennareddy said. He gave the example of someone who gains 20 pounds, loses 30 and then gains 20 again. “That is even more detrimental,” he said.When people lose weight, the body slows its resting metabolism, he said. When the weight comes back, “most of the weight they gain is fat, not muscle,” he said. Even someone who loses and regains 5% to 7% of their body weight may end up with slightly less muscle and more fat, he said.Some research has shown that weight fluctuation is associated with a higher risk of high blood pressure and cardiovascular disease-related death.

The study’s weight changes took place between about 2008 and 2013, according to the study’s timeline.

Recent findings suggest that wegovy, a GLP-1 medication for weight management, rolled out in the United Kingdom in September 2023, according to the UK Department of Health and Social Care.Cunningham said the weight-cycling findings raised questions for people who take GLP-1 medications. She said drugmakers’ own data show that “once you get off of those, your weight is going to go right back to where it was before, possibly even worse.”That could create the same up-and-down pattern, Cunningham said. She added that researchers don’t yet know “what happens in the really long term” for people who take these medications.

The study highlighted links between weight changes and heart health and cannot prove that weight changes caused the results, according to the authors. They wrote that the small number of people who lost weight made those results less precise.Bridger-Staatz also stated the team did not look at why or how people lost weight.

In a recent development, cunningham said adults lose muscle and bone mass with age, and that the loss is especially pronounced for women in their 50s and older. “Maintaining muscles and maintaining bones is so, so important,” she said.Staying active helps people keep muscle, even without weight loss, Cunningham said. “Even a little bit of activity…just keep moving,” she said.GLP-1 medications work best as part of a “comprehensive proposal,” Chennareddy said. With his patients, he said he recommends continuous improvement rather than setting a goal to lose a specific amount of weight within a set period.Patients who treat weight loss as “a gradual process” do better long term, he said.“The most important thing is not to do fad diets,” Chennareddy said.For people losing weight, Chennareddy recommended:.

Anyone considering changes to their weight can talk with a healthcare professional about their weight history and goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

According to recent reports, I was running out to grab a cup of coffee and asked my co-worker if I could grab one for her. No biggie, just a common courtesy. I literally didn’t even go out of my way. But when I returned, she couldn't have been more grateful. Sometimes when we do small, simple things, we realize later how much they meant to others.

It could be something like a thoughtful message or a quick check-in where we take a few minutes to listen.

It has been revealed that the thing is, we often underestimate the impact of these simple gestures. We are all so busy these days, caught up in daily responsibilities and checking all the boxes to complete everything on our list, that we tend to forget how much we can effortlessly offer to others.

Industry observers note that of course, in this fast-paced world, we are always striving for more from life. And, at the same time, it's important to pause and recognize what we have and how it can be shared with those around us.

Just take a moment to think about some of the people who make a difference in your life. Perhaps it was that friend who checked in on you during a difficult time or a supervisor who encouraged you. They may not have given their generosity much thought, but I bet you remember how it made you feel, right?

Recent findings suggest that let me share with you a research study that supports this idea. A 2023 study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found that people frequently underestimate how positive acts of kindness impact others. In one study, participants who gave strangers hot chocolate thought the recipients would be happy, but in reality, the recipients were incredibly grateful for the gesture.

It has been revealed that generativity, a concept developed by psychologist Erik Erikson, describes how a person wants to contribute to the lives of others and make a difference for future generations. This is evidenced in the things that we do, like mentoring others, supporting a friend or family member, or sharing lessons.

In a recent development, it’s notable to mention that the research demonstrates a strong connection between helping people and well-being. In 2020, Psychological Bulletin published a meta-analysis of more than 200 studies and found a consistent relationship between helping people and positive well-being.

It’s notable to mention that giving to others doesn't mean we are neglecting our needs. It just means that we are also helping one another build relationships. And the research also shows that a sense of connection really matters.

Sadly, we are often so busy managing all that we have to do that we don't think about how we can support others.

So, let’s take a few minutes to reflect:.

It has been revealed that which of these options could you incorporate into your schedule this week? (Choose just one.) You will both benefit if you reach out, offer a little encouragement, listen, or just let someone know they are on your mind. The point is that it doesn't have to be this massive grand gesture. Small acts of kindness go a long way.

Life's most meaningful moments happen with people who took the time to listen, remember, or encourage, or helped us feel less alone. Don’t wait for more time or money, or until you've figured everything out, before you try to make a difference. Just start with where you are.

Recent findings suggest that take a moment and think about one small act of kindness that was bestowed upon you. How can you do the same for others?

As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.

In a recent development, xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The company isn’t going it alone, however.

Xiomi is working local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive, rather than operating its own retail network, with Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirming that the company would officially enter Western car markets next year at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen held 17NOV.

CarNewsChina reports that Gargash Prime Automotive is offering 13 variants across the Xiaomi SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup, with retail prices starting at 169,900 AED ($~46,200 US) for the SU7 Standard and climbing all the way up to 375,900 AED ($~102,000 US) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra.

Not to lump a bunch of nations with their own rich heritage and car culture together, but it’s fair to say that drivers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait love their supercars – and the brand’s Xiaomi SU7 Ultra might be one of the most super of them all, thanks to fully 1,548 hp from three high-torque electric motors, the SU7 Ultra can sprint from 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in under two seconds on its way to a towering, 217 mph top speed.

In a recent development, it’s not just a straight-line speed machine, either. Xiaomi gave its go-fast flagship a serious track-focused makeover on its way to becomig the “Utlra,” complete with carbon-ceramic brakes, an aggressive (if controversial) composite aero package, an enormous rear wing, and a chassis tuned to tackle the turns the Green Hell of the Nürburgring.

And, at a relatively reasonable $102,000 equivalent price, I’d be willing to bet that a lot of the hypercar-loving Emiratis will be eager to get their hands on one.

The first customer deliveries of the Xiaomi SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro models are scheduled for December of this year, with deliveries of the remaining variants scheduled for February 2027.

Fresh electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development claims the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • Sources indicate that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s consumers were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development claims the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

Sources indicate that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team notes that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

Industry observers note that the shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

Recent findings suggest that researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

The potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

Scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

In a recent development, finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

It has been revealed that those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team says more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

It’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike stated in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

Last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that showed intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

“Fiona was such a gift,” mentioned Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Recent findings suggest that fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

#155789. Breaking: 5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (967 w)

Breaking: 5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to.
  • Recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to. Consider the feelings that come up for you when you think about it. Is it excitement about seeing the people you love? Is it dread at the anticipation of planning, conflict, or grief? For some, it’s all of the above.

Recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S. adults report holiday stressors (APA, 2023). Tensions arise due to finances, family conflict, grief, and other factors. Stress takes away from the pleasurable aspects of the season, which should include reconnection and rest.

In a recent development, sometimes that is easier noted than done. Here are 5 things we're saying no to this holiday season and strategies to achieve the happy holidays we deserve.

Sometimes that family holiday announcement sounds like a demand rather than an invitation. “Dinner is at 4 pm sharp. See you there!” Everyone assumes you’ll be there, and no one asks questions. They don’t ask if you can take time off work, afford the trip, or have other prepares. You feel obligated to attend despite any barriers you are facing.

It has been revealed that almost no one will tell you that you are allowed to consider your own needs before you RSVP yes. Ask yourself whether you have the time, energy, and money to participate this year. If the answer is no, it’s alright. Your family may be disappointed, and you may feel a little guilty, but it’s worth asking which will weigh on you more: the guilt of saying no or the cost of saying yes.

Sources indicate that in toxic families, it’s the once-over as soon as you enter the room. Before you’ve even had a chance to sit down, someone has made a joke about your weight or graying hair, offered a backhanded compliment about the dish you contributed, or slipped in a dig about your personal life.

It has been revealed that you may feel hurt, sad, or even angry, and you don’t have to ignore those feelings to preserve the holiday spirit. You can be silent and stone-faced to let the “joke” fall flat. You might excuse yourself and regroup in another room. If you want to address it directly and call out the hidden meaning, you can say, “That felt like a dig,” or ask, “What do you mean by that?” What you don’t have to do is tolerate disrespect.

According to recent reports, when you want everyone to feel loved, it’s easy to slip into spending more than you intended. If you’ve ever hosted a large family gathering, you know how quickly the groceries and gifts add up. And if you’re the one who hosts every year, it can feel like the work and the bill are yours by default.

According to recent reports, before you do anything, set a budget. Then share the work in ways that play into everyone’s strengths. Maybe enlist the nephew who can roast meat or the cousin who loves to bake, and assign cleanup to the one you prefer to stay out of the kitchen. Suggest rotating hosting duties. Do a gift exchange rather than buying individual gifts for everyone. You can show your love to your family with limits.

Sources indicate that in some families, playing the dutiful daughter (or son) means everyone assumes you’ll make the holidays happen. Often it’s the family matriarch or the eldest daughter who initiates the first call about the holiday looks and is the one still in the kitchen long after everyone else has gone home. She is the family “glue” who keeps track of the invites, remembers who can’t eat what, and figures out where to seat the relatives who aren’t speaking. By the time the holiday arrives, she’s too tired to enjoy the fruits of her labor.

If that sounds like you, name it. People who have never hosted may not realize all of the hidden effort that goes into an event. Bring it to their attention. Set limits on what you will do and ask for help, but don’t micromanage. If the person assigned to bring the rolls forgets, skip the rolls this year. If no one steps up, step back anyway. Proposal a smaller, more intimate gathering that won’t leave you frazzled at the end of it.

Sources indicate that the holidays aren’t the same after you’ve lost a loved one, and the first holiday season after a loss can be especially difficult. Family traditions may be upended. The person who always hosted and made everyone’s favorite dish is gone. Tensions that surface after the loss may still be hanging in the air.

Take a moment to evaluate your feelings. Ask yourself what you feel up to this year. Maybe it’s not the year to take on hosting duties, or perhaps you stop by for dessert rather than staying the entire day. You can choose to honor your loved one by retaining old traditions or step into the next chapter with new traditions in their memory. You can miss someone deeply and still make room for moments of joy this holiday season.

It might seem strange that saying no could be the start of a happy holiday. The beauty is that you get to decide what a happy holiday looks like for you, and that it can change from year to year. Ask yourself what would make the holidays feel good to you this year and do it.

In a recent development, american Psychological Association. (2023). Even a joyous holiday season can cause stress for most Americans. https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2023/11/holiday-season-stress.

#155788. Why Cancer Biomarker Testing Is Personal for Mark-Paul Gosselaar

📅 02 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1097 w)

Why Cancer Biomarker Testing Is Personal for Mark-Paul Gosselaar

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.
  • Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.
  • According to recent reports, “Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.

Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.

According to recent reports, “Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline. “We are constantly aware of newly introduced technologies.”.

Having seen people in his life navigate cancer diagnoses, Gosselaar is now raising awareness about the role of biomarker testing in cancer treatment through his partnership with AstraZeneca and its Meet Your Mark campaign.

The campaign aims to educate people facing cancer diagnoses and their loved ones about how biomarker testing may help doctors make more informed, personalized treatment decisions. It also encourages patients to discuss testing with their healthcare teams.

“Biomarkers may tell doctors the specific type of cancer present and if targeted therapies or immunotherapy might help,” Mark Socinski, MD, oncologist and Executive Medical Director of the AdventHealth Cancer Institute, told Healthline.

He explained that biomarkers are typically genes or proteins that doctors measure through blood or tissue tests. They are used to help guide treatment in numerous diseases but are especially powerful tools in many types of cancer.

Sources indicate that “They help decode why cancers behave differently, even when two people have the same cancer type,” stated Socinski. “However, while biomarker testing provides useful information, it does not guarantee a specific outcome.”.

Despite those limitations, Socinski sees promise in the shift from one-size-fits-all cancer treatment to care tailored to each patient’s specific cancer characteristics.

In a recent development, “Biomarker testing does play a critical role here, and it is notable for people to be aware of the potential benefits,” Socinski said. “It may help change the course of a person’s treatment journey.”.

Gosselaar hopes that greater awareness of biomarker testing can help people facing a cancer diagnosis feel more informed about their treatment options.

“A lot of the time, when a loved one or someone who has been diagnosed with cancer [it can] feel like your world is in a tailspin,” he said. “I wanted to get the word out for anyone who’s going through a cancer diagnosis, or a caretaker, to know that biomarker testing is an option, because even though two cancers are similar, their tumors can act very differently and biomarker testing may help the medical expert with more personalized treatment.”.

As part of the campaign, Gosselaar took part in a commercial, something he hadn’t done since before his days on “Saved by the Bell.”.

“This was the first time that I actually had to be on set and not be a character; I had to be me talking about this very serious matter,” he said.

While it was a challenging experience, he noted it was also fulfilling.

“I enjoyed the process, and to be able to use my platform to be able to spread the word; it means a lot to me,” he said. “I’m very selective of the things that I want to attach myself to, and this seemed like the right fit.”.

He particularly enjoyed recreating Zack Morris’s signature “timeout” gesture from “Saved by the Bell,” which allowed his character to freeze time and speak directly to the camera.

“Using something from the past that was such a symbolic gesture to so many people of my generation that are now my age and possibly going through [cancer] or knowing someone who’s going through [cancer to] direct them to [this campaign], means a lot,” he said.

Beyond his efforts to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing, Gosselaar is equally focused on taking care of his own health.

Getting quality sleep is one of his top priorities. He sleeps on a high-tech mattress that monitors sleep stages, heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate. He also uses a biometric health and fitness tracker, prioritizes healthy eating, and uses saunas and red light therapy.

“We do everything that we possibly can, but I’m less about longevity and more about just living a healthy lifestyle,” Gosselaar remarked. “I want to continue doing the things that I’ve done since I was a child…without feeling held back by my health.”.

According to recent reports, as he embraces his 50s, he remarked he’d like to live a long life for his children and future grandchildren. He started taking his health seriously in his 40s after undergoing shoulder surgery.

“[It] really made me realize [that] all the damage I had done in my 20s and 30s sort of adds up later in life, and that’s probably something that I would tell the younger me… to preserve a little bit more and take [an] approach that recovery is just as crucial as the workout because I did not use my recovery very well; it was not a priority for me,” remarked Gosselaar.

In a recent development, he also makes time for himself every day. He remarked doing so makes him a better person and more able to care for his wife and four children.

According to recent reports, “[It’s] something that I believe in; that I need to do something for myself before I can do something for someone else. Or if I do something for someone else, then I have to equalize that by doing something for me,” he said.

Daily physical activity also helps support his mental well-being.

It has been revealed that “I need to do something where I challenge myself, and it could be as simple as a walk. It could be as simple as just getting outside and lifting something heavy [or] taking bags of groceries and taking the long way into your house,” Gosselaar noted.

“Like challenging yourself with picking up things, you know, taking backpacks from the car from your kids and seeing if you can carry three in one hand…or going into the gym and spending an hour in the gym, or 30 minutes, or just moving.”.

When he’s in the sauna, he works on breathing and clearing his thoughts.

Industry observers note that “Some people need to meditate, some people need to talk to somebody. I encourage all of that because I think all of that helps,” he stated.

Recent findings suggest that the world said goodbye to Fiona the hippo on Thursday. Fiona died at age 9 after ingesting a knit hat.

In a recent development, fiona captivated the world since her birth in 2017. She beat the odds after being born six weeks premature and weighing only 29 pounds. Her tiny stature and determined, playful nature made her an extraordinarily popular resident of the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden.

“Fiona was such a gift,” said Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

To celebrate Fiona’s life, the zoo shared a collection of Fiona images from over the years—from her early days as a spunky calf to her more recent hippo shenanigans. Scroll down for some of our favorite videos of Fiona too.

This story was updated at 4:37 am EST on 11/27/26 to reflect Black Friday pricing.

According to recent reports, the Black Friday furniture deals are going strong, and we’ve rounded up a hearty list of discounts that are so tasty they may just overshadow grandma’s famous pumpkin pie leftovers. No matter where you lie on the design spectrum—coastal, midcentury, farmhouse—there’s an upgrade for you at a price that’s more than palatable. Some of our favorite brands have rolled out discounts on living room furniture, bedroom sets, and statement pieces that have absolutely no business being in our shopping cart but somehow end up there anyway. Considering how promptly foundational pieces like a newly introduced sofa, bed frame, or dresser can gobble up a decorating budget, we’re certainly not complaining.

We’ve highlighted the brands offering big deals for you to take advantage of. So fret not—that statement area rug or lovely sectional sofa you were hoping to score for a fraction of the price is well within reach! Bookmark this page, we’ll be updating it as more Black Friday furniture deals go live.

There comes a hellish time in all lives where it becomes clear the living room needs a bit of a refresh—a potentially pricey undertaking. The good news is that if we’re tactful about it, any upgrades can be up to 70% off thanks to Black Friday sales. In search of a latest sectional? We’ve tested them extensively. Need a good reading chair to tie it altogether? We’ve tested those, too. We have guides to consoles, coffee tables, a hefty piece on Black Friday rug sales. Basically, whatever you need—we’ve got some recommendations. Here’s our best-of list for high-quality, stylish pieces at a fraction of their price.

Not everyone has the time to wait for a solid oak heirloom to fall into their lap, and these dignified pieces are worthwhile alternatives. Whether you have a dedicated dining room (you lucky dog), or a tiny kitchen that needs to pull double duty, the right dining table for you is on mega sale so you can host big parties at home regardless of space constraints. Our favorite deal? An extra 25% off the Elle dining table from Lulu & Georgia makes it an even better buy.

Sources indicate that there’s something you should probably know about us: We love sleep. So much so that we've tested upwards of 30 mattresses and sleep-related products, all in the name of making sure you have recommendations you can rely on. Black Friday is very much the time to invest in a mattress at a discounted price if you're looking to enter the new year with a better sleep report from your smartwatch, but we don’t think you should neglect the remainder of your bedroom. With that in mind, we’ve rounded up a few great deals on bed frames, dressers, nightstands, and even a few bedding deals to have you waking up on the right side of the bed in 2027.

Industry observers note that while the weather outside is frightful, the deals on outdoor furniture are just the opposite. One of our favorite outdoor brands, Neighbor, has slashed 15% sitewide, so teak and wicker finds are now within budget’s reach. Outer is also offering 30% on its full teak sets, outdoor umbrellas, fire pit setups, and you can even score additional patio pieces for free at a certain purchase point. When spring returns, finally, you’ll be ready to celebrate.

According to recent reports, one of our favorite gifting hubs, Anthropologie, also stocks a surprisingly robust assortment of furniture and decor. The brand is even running a furniture-specific promotion of up to 30% off lots of current season home goods. The Irena tufted sofa is what English cottage dreams are made of—so much so we’re in the mood for another rewatch of The Holiday to swoon over 2000’s Jude Law. If you’ve got a robust collection of tchotchkes that deserve their own moment, the Fern storage cabinet is the perfect way to help them shine.

According to recent reports, makers of American classics, Arhaus is running discounts across all of their departments. Whether you're looking for holiday decor or a hefty sectional, Arhaus has got a sale going. Contributor Lila Allen instantly fell in love with her Kipton sofa, “The combo of soft curves and clean and modern lines make this a really versatile piece,” Lila stated. “My apartment is eclectic, and it fit right in with our existing decor—so consider this a solid example of transitional style. I think it could work well in a Scandi, contemporary, or boho space.”.

Lulu and Georgia's sale includes up to 30% off sitewide on offerings like the AD-reviewed (and loved) Cleary sofa, but we also recommend digging into all the clearance furniture and decor collections for an extra 25% off already discounted gems. Whether you’re looking for something like upcoming dinnerware to anchor your holiday tablescape, or a Mandy Moore-approved outdoor item to save for next year, you have lots of options.

A good night’s sleep is an invaluable investment, but that doesn't mean you have to pay full price for it. Saatva is currently offering up to $625 off orders, giving you a head start on upgrading your sleep set up if a luxurious mattress is on your wishlist. Note: You need a mattress in your cart for the discount to apply. The Loom & Leaf is particularly attractive for memory foam devotees, which contributor Bailey Berg previously described as the “most breathable, comfortable mattress” she’d ever tried. And if a bedroom overhaul is in the cards, Saatva’s upholstered Halle storage platform bed offers a discreet place to stash extra bedding totally out of sight.

A little coastal influence can go a long way, even if the nearest beach is blanketed in snow during the off-season. Serena & Lily is at the moment hosting The Sale of the Year, with up to 40% off furniture, mirrors, and lighting, plus discounts across nearly every other product category. It’s a chance to bring the brand’s breezy, tailored aesthetic home in time for the holidays. We’re particularly fond of its outdoor lineup, including the Pacifica Sofa, which AD contributor Blake Bakkila put to the test for more than three years at her Newport Beach home. Despite its exposure to coastal moisture, she reported no fading, warping, or damage, and gave the sofa an overall A rating. For an indoor refresh, the Carter counter stool brings the brand’s signature natural texture into the kitchen.

Industry observers note that there’s a reason Wayfair is a go-to destination when a room needs furnishing without a designer-size budget. The retailer’s Holiday Flash Sale is underway, with discounts of up to 70% sitewide. Its family of brands includes AllModern, a favorite for contemporary silhouettes at relatively approachable prices. AD contributor Elise Portale tested the AllModern Breanna chaise sectional, praising its soft upholstery. “At the end of the day, the best way I can describe it is ‘luxurious,’” she stated. Take your living room refresh a step further with a ladder bookcase from Madison Park, or get a head start on decking the halls with festive finds at wallet-friendly prices.

According to recent reports, article is offering up to 40% off on select pieces across their vast catalogue of midcentury-inspired furnishings and decor, meaning now’s your chance to snag a deal on this plush loveseat sectional that won’t overwhelm smaller spaces. Another A+ find? A nifty side table with discreet storage we’ve written about before.

A design classic rarely comes cheap, which makes Design Within Reach’s sale particularly noteworthy. Right now, you can score 25% off iconic furniture silhouettes and 30% off task and gaming chairs. For a home office that deserves a little more consideration than the average desk-and-chair combination, look to the Eames Soft Pad Management Chair or George Nelson’s Swag Leg Desk. Think of this as your sign to incorporate a little bit of legendary mid-century design into your workday for a fraction of the price.

Crate & Barrel’s designer collaborations are reason enough to redecorate, but throw in a 30% off Accent Furniture Sale and deeply discounted clearance finds, and the temptation is harder to resist. We’ve been drawn to the collection created by actor Laura Harrier and interior designer Tiffany Howell, which debuted in April and pairs richly layered materials and vintage influences to contemporary furniture. Their Siren queen bed is right now 33% off, or you can snag Jake Arnold’s Sculptural Metal Accent Chair for 20% off, among other hidden gems.

In a recent development, joybird’s extensive upholstery catalog and seemingly endless configuration options make up for every sad millennial-gray starter sofa that’s seen one move too many. The brand’s Black Friday sale offers up to 45% off select furniture, including its distinctive, customizable seating. AD senior entertainment editor Rachel Wallace chose the Sebastian sofa in a vibrant chartreuse velvet and was won over by its rounded silhouette and generous proportions. “This is by far the most supreme nap sofa I have ever experienced,” she said. The Sebastian is just one of many seating options worth considering, along with the Amelia grand swivel chair, a cozy contender for reading nooks and movie nights.

Amazon’s furniture selection can require some digging, but there are worthwhile finds among the seemingly endless listings, particularly for bedroom basics. Allewie is among our favorite furniture brands on Amazon, and deals on its already affordable pieces can save you up to 33%. The brand’s lift-up hydraulic storage bed frame is an especially practical pick for bedrooms short on closet space, offering concealed storage beneath the mattress. “I think the best part of the frame is that it takes up a good amount of space without being excessive, allowing for a good variety of bedroom setup,” states contributor Will Porter, who tested the bed frame at home. The brand’s black oak wooden bed frame takes a more understated approach with a sleek, modern headboard and footboard, but don’t stop there. Amazon has plenty of discounted furniture for the rest of your home, too.

It has been revealed that shea McGee has the magic touch for making spaces feel collected and curated, and McGee & Co.’s furniture reflects the designer’s signature sensibility. The brand’s current sale features up to 70% off select pieces, with substantial reductions on dining chairs, end tables, nightstands, and bedroom furniture. The Beacon nightstand is 40% off, and the Gilmore canopy bed, a modern minimalist’s dream, is marked down to its lowest price ever. These contemporary heirlooms are more likely to be passed down from one generation to the next than they are to go out of style, so these prices are practically a steal.

In a recent development, west Elm is hosting The Fall Sale, offering up to 60% off plus an extra 20% off select styles. The brand’s midcentury-inspired dressers and nightstands are perennial favorites, but we’re particularly interested in the Shelter Sleeper sofa for anyone expecting out-of-town guests this holiday season. Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert tested the queen-size version in dark olive performance velvet and called it “the softest, cushiest couch in my house.” Another standout from the sale is the midcentury five-drawer dresser, a handsome storage solution narrow enough for smaller bedrooms and cozy apartments. Equally impressive deals can be found on accent chairs, dining tables, and some of the brand’s bestsellers.

Pottery Barn’s extensive selection of living room, dining room, and bedroom furniture has earned it a reputation as a one-stop shop for furnishing an entire space. Its current Fall Sale includes up to 70% of select furniture, with additional discounts on certain styles. The brand is known for its comfortable, traditional seating, including the York Slope Arm Deep Seat Slipcovered Side Sleeper, currently 20% off. Contributor Kate McGregor tested the sofa and praised its plush cushions, washable slipcover, and easy-to-use sleeper mechanism. “This is one of the most comfortable sofas I’ve had the pleasure of sitting on,” she wrote. If your living room doubles as your guest room, this is one deal you won’t want to skip.

It has been revealed that perusing Nickey Kehoe’s sale section is akin to sifting through buried treasure. The Los Angeles design studio and retailer is known for furniture that feels thoughtful, rich with character, and difficult to pin to any one decorating era. Its Last Chance section offers up to 30% off distinctive pieces like the architectural Iron Canopy Bed and the Community Harvest Bench. Both have the kind of lived-in appeal that makes a room look as though it’s been furnished gradually, with pieces collected over time.
